data.plain: Files Microcosm writes about itself get no exemptions. Its standards, paper modules, ledgers, routes, generated pages and release claims must meet the same evidence, anti-claim and refusal requirements they apply to everything else.

analogy.boundary: The calibration picture covers equal treatment only; it does not tell you whether the lab's instruments are accurate.

maps.analogy: the same standard applied to customers' equipment
maps.doctrine: the same rules applied to the work it audits

maps.analogy: no looser rule for the lab's own gauges
maps.doctrine: no exemption for the system's own documents

analogy.text: A calibration lab's own instruments must pass the same calibration check the lab applies to its customers' equipment, with no looser rule for its own gauges.

reader.counterexample: The system publishes a self-assessment calling its own work verified and complete, in wording that would fail the evidence rules it applies to the components it audits.
reader.does_not_prove: Meeting its own rules removes a double standard; it does not make the system complete or ready.

example.text: The release wording gate applies the same claim-language rules to the system's own public copy as to any other component, so overclaiming wording in a self-description is blocked at release.

reader.governs: Claims the system makes about itself.
reader.plain: When the system describes or assesses itself, that description has to meet exactly the same evidence and honesty standard it enforces on everything else.
reader.potential_misread: That a system describing itself can be taken at its word, or that meeting the standard makes its self-description correct.
reader.refuses: A lighter standard for the system's own documents than for the work they audit.
reader.requires: Holding standards, paper modules, ledgers, routes, generated pages and release wording to the same evidence, stated-limit and refusal rules as any other component.
reader.why_it_matters: A system's statements about itself are where overclaiming hides most easily, so holding them to the same rules keeps its public limits honest.
